P05.title: Geometry 101 part 2 · frame vs handlebar numbers

ig.caption:
Geometry charts list frame stack and reach. But you don't hold the frame. You hold the handlebar.

Between the two sit the spacers (they lift the bars) and the stem (it pushes them forward).

Canyon Grail Gen 2 (M) vs Specialized Crux (56), on the chart: the Grail frame is 13 mm taller and 14 mm longer.

As sold, the Grail has a 70 mm stem and the Crux a 100 mm stem. So at the handlebar the Crux puts your hands 16 mm further forward (486 vs 470 mm).

16 mm further = a lower, more stretched position. Great if you're flexible, harder on a stiff back and neck. Neither bike is better. It's about which one fits you.

Geomo scores every bike as it's sold, with the factory stem and typical spacers, and shows frame and handlebar numbers side by side. If a different stem would fit you better, it tells you.

P07.title: Geometry 101 part 3 · handling

ig.caption:
Fit is how you sit. Geometry also decides how a bike rides. Five numbers worth knowing:

Head angle (HTA): slacker = calmer, steeper = quicker steering. Gravel bikes in size M: 69.5° to 72°.

Trail: more = holds a line, less = turns in fast. Published values: 59 to 86 mm.

Wheelbase: longer = steadier, shorter = nimbler. 1011 to 1082 mm.

Chainstay: short = lively, long = planted, with room for big tyres. 420 to 450 mm.

BB drop: more = you sit lower and steadier, but with less room for rocks and a pedal that can touch down mid-corner. Less = more clearance, a bit less steady. 65 to 83 mm.

Neither end is better. It depends on how and where you ride.

In Geomo, fit % comes first. The Target score then adds handling, so you find a bike that fits and rides the way you want. Free, no account. Link in bio.

P16.title: P16 reel · Two sizes fit. Which one? · Notatnik (zaakceptowany w harmonogramie; Maciej 13.11: podmień wszystko)

ig.caption:
Two sizes fit. Which one?

On a Canyon Grail Gen 3, a 178 cm rider (inseam 84 cm) gets 98% in S with a 90 mm stem and 98% in M with a 70 mm stem. Same hand position. So how do you choose?

Size down if you like quick, playful handling (the S is 23 mm shorter between the wheels) or want room to ride lower later (32 mm of spacers to remove).

Size up if you want a calmer ride, long days with bags, or a tidier front end (same bar height with 13 mm fewer spacers).

Same score? Pick the one that rides like you do. Geomo shows both sizes and the stem each one needs. Free, no account. Link in bio.

P14.title: P14 reel · Black Friday 1/3: parts you can swap · Notatnik (Maciej 13.11: P14 OK - podmień)

ig.caption:
Black Friday is coming. Before you look at discounts, look at this.

Tyres, saddle, stem and bar, gearing, wheels: you can swap all of them later.

Stack, reach, head angle, wheelbase: those are built into the frame. You live with them for as long as you own the bike.

Spacers, stem length and a steeper (negative) stem can fine-tune the fit. A −17° stem instead of −6° drops the bars about 11 mm. But one size up on a gravel bike is typically 20 mm taller and 9 mm longer.

The part you can't swap usually costs the most. Check your size before you check the price. Free, no account. Link in bio.

P18.title: P18 · Black Friday 3/3: 60 seconds before you pay · Notatnik (Maciej 12.11: podmień w automacie)

ig.caption:
Black Friday checklist for bike deals. 60 seconds before you pay:

1. Know your body: your inseam (barefoot, book between your legs, floor to spine) and how flexible you are. Same 178 cm rider, stiff vs flexible: the ideal handlebar moves 58 mm.
2. Ignore the letter. A size M gravel frame can have a stack anywhere from 552 to 607 mm.
3. Check where your hands end up: frame + spacers + stock stem.
4. Between sizes? Check both. Same bike, same rider: 95% in M, 54% in L.
5. Wrong size? Skip the deal. A stem is cheap. A frame isn't.

Geomo runs checks 2–4 for you in about a minute. Free, no account. Link in bio.
